boundaries.name: Create to match
boundaries.description: The title and the formulas that apply to it are one invocation.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: Someone types what they are about to do and reads what applies.
boundaries.causalityJustification: A match printed after the work began is a runbook nobody opened. The match must come back in the same breath as the title.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The applying formulas appear under the created work item, immediately.

boundaries.name: dotdiw to the tracker
boundaries.description: dotdiw reaches the tracker through an adapter behind the inner door: a store in its own process, the tracker binary as a local subprocess, or a hosted tracker over its network. Typed records cross; a forwarded command's stream crosses only under the beads adapter.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: A pour becomes one tracker issue per step.
boundaries.causalityJustification: The acknowledgement is immediate; creating the issues is the tracker's work and may take longer than a second.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The poured steps are visible in the tracker once the pour returns.

boundaries.name: Check to report
boundaries.description: A local search over the project's own text, reported at once.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: The project asks whether its formulas can be found.
boundaries.causalityJustification: The answer is computed from files already on disk; nothing justifies waiting for it.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: One line per formula that cannot be found, or one line saying all can.

boundaries.name: Repository to remote
boundaries.description: A formula reaches other people the way every other file does: by being committed, pushed and pulled.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: A committed formula is shared through git.
boundaries.causalityJustification: Sharing is git's. dotdiw adds nothing of its own, so the formula is held by the project when git holds it.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: Everyone's next create can reach the formula once they have pulled it.

boundaries.name: Adoption
boundaries.description: One command, run once, on one machine, for one checkout -- a key in its .git/config, a tracker under the home, the declaration in its tree.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: A repository is given tracking under the home and the two conventions in its tree.
boundaries.causalityJustification: Adoption is local and complete when the command returns; nothing of it happens elsewhere or later.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: Two files in the repository, which are the worker's to commit, and one directory under the home, ~/.dotdiw/<key>.

boundaries.name: Run any command
boundaries.description: The housekeeping around a command happens in the same process, before or after it, on this machine.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: A config file and a git setting are read; one small write where something needs undoing.
boundaries.causalityJustification: Metrics must be off before the first tracker command of the run, and a hook override must be gone before the worker's next commit; neither can be deferred past the command it precedes.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: Nothing, except a notice the first time something was turned off or undone.

boundaries.name: Command to tracker
boundaries.description: A command the worker typed reaches the tracker: the interface's own are answered by the chosen adapter; under beads any other reaches the binary as a local subprocess and its output comes back through dotdiw's rewrite.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: The tracker runs the command; dotdiw streams the answer back without the tracker's name.
boundaries.causalityJustification: dotdiw owns only the spawn and the stream; the tracker's own latency is whatever it is, from a list to an init.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The tracker's answer, under dotdiw's name, with interactive prompts still working.

boundaries.name: List to answer
boundaries.description: The project's formulas are found on the file system and read from disk, answered at once.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: Someone asks what the project holds, or names a formula by id.
boundaries.causalityJustification: The answer is a walk of the tree and a few small files; nothing justifies waiting for it or asking anything outside the repository.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The formulas the project holds, with their paths, or one formula's text.

boundaries.name: Provider to answer
boundaries.description: A registered provider lists its formulas, asked once per process, and shows one when it is shown or poured.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: A file system or an API endpoint answers list and show.
boundaries.causalityJustification: dotdiw waits for each provider's answer, asked once per process. A provider takes what its store takes, a directory read or a call to an endpoint, and how fresh its formulas are across processes is its own.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The provider's formulas beside the local ones, or one line naming a provider left out of the run.

boundaries.name: Learn to text
boundaries.description: The teaching text is compiled into the tool and printed.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: Someone reads how work gets done here.
boundaries.causalityJustification: There is nothing to wait for; the text is in the binary.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The four capabilities and the two conventions, in full.

boundaries.name: New to file
boundaries.description: The starting file for a tracker is written from text compiled into the tool.
boundaries.realWorldProcess: Someone starts a tracker of their own.
boundaries.causalityJustification: There is nothing to wait for; the text is in the tool, and the file is small.
boundaries.userVisibleImpact: The path written, and the check to run next.

externalProductDependencies.reason: beads is a tracker a checkout may choose, installed on its own: under that choice it holds the work items, cooks and pours formulas, and owns every command dotdiw forwards. dotdiw adds discovery and hides the second name. It is reached only through the beads adapter, behind the tracker door; the interface is what dotdiw's bodies see.
externalProductDependencies.boundarySemantics: A local subprocess on the same machine, run by the beads adapter alone, told where its state lives through BEADS_DIR: ~/.dotdiw/<key>/.beads under the user's home, keyed to the checkout. It runs in its stealth mode with hooks and agent files declined, so it commits nothing, writes nothing into the repository and configures no remote. The adapter turns its usage metrics off before the first call, rewrites its name in everything it prints, and otherwise changes nothing it does. It has no POA IDL; the commands below are what the adapter calls.
calledOperations: every command dotdiw does not own, forwarded unchanged

externalProductDependencies.reason: git is the sharing mechanism: a formula the project holds is one git tracks, and it reaches other people as every other file does. The project's tracked text is read from it as the background the formulas are ranked against; the formulas themselves are found on the file system.
externalProductDependencies.boundarySemantics: The project's own repository, read and never written except two lines inside its .git/config -- the key under which this checkout's tracker lives, and the adapter it was chosen to go through, local to the clone and never in the tree: dotdiw lists tracked and untracked files, reads and unsets one hooks key that an earlier version let the tracker set, and reads status for the declaration files. For a tracker check it makes a scratch repository of its own under a temporary directory and removes it. It never commits, pushes, syncs or changes the index. It has no POA IDL; the commands below are what dotdiw calls.

openQuestions.question: The threshold of 0.15 was calibrated on three to fifty-six formulas. What do retrieval and silence look like at the hundreds this is for?
Should a project be able to tell, per piece of work, that it began unnamed, or does that cross from showing into enforcing?

updates.summary: Derived Product Operation IDL from model.dotdiw.
updates.reason: The product model needs an operation algebra before implementation and projection.

updates.summary: Reference the contract that witnesses a named piece of work finding its procedure, bind the observed labels to the operations that emit them, and make any report or summary of discovery firing answer to it.
updates.reason: A claim that discovery fired must be backed by a witness contract, not by an invocation log read by hand.

updates.summary: Replace the generated poa invoke bindings with dotdiw's real command line, bind every operation to one inline body in dotdiw through promise_bindings.py, declare beads and git as the products dotdiw calls and name the calls, correct the kinds the step-id heuristic got wrong, and give the request and response types the fields the bodies use.
updates.reason: Until the bindings are real, POA checks the artifacts against each other and never against the program. These are the facts that let it check the program.

updates.summary: Invoke every operation through one door generated from the IDL into dotdiw: the request held to its type on the way in, the response to its own on the way out, the witness log appended and the terminal fed from the typed response, with the request and response types made true to what the bodies use. Migration plan: none; nothing a worker sees changes, and seventeen commands print the same bytes as before.
updates.reason: A body bound to the IDL in name only read fields its type never declared, printed what no response carried and wrote the witness log itself, and nothing noticed. Through one door the types are the contract, every transport runs the same bodies, and the tests hold the program to the IDL from its source.

updates.summary: Put the tracker behind a door of its own: the ten operations of a tracker interface, with typed requests and responses, generated into dotdiw as a second table and answered by an adapter chosen per request, else per workspace, else the shipped default, with one implementation binding per adapter for each. Two adapters ship: local, a sqlite store under the workspace's keyed directory and the default for a new adoption, and beads, the tracker of every version before, kept to its bytes; a third, for Jira Cloud, is loaded by name from the home and proved against a stub. Four operations list, choose, check and migrate. Migration plan: a workspace adopted by an earlier version is pinned to beads by its first command and told so once; nothing a worker who chose nothing sees changes, and under beads the same twenty commands print the same bytes; dotdiw tracker migrate moves a workspace between adapters, ids kept where the target accepts them and mapped in a record under the workspace where it does not, the source never written.
updates.reason: Eight bodies reached one tracker by name through two runners and a stream rewrite, and the IDL named the product and its calls without an interface a second tracker could answer. Behind a door of its own the interface is the record: every adapter is held to the same types by the door and to the same scenario by the conformance suite, the bodies cross nowhere but the door, and a worker can choose a tracker, or none, without dotdiw changing.

updates.summary: A module is looked for in the home directory and then in share/dotdiw/trackers beside the tool; it says which interface it was written for, and any other is refused by name when it loads; dotdiw tracker check takes a file by path; dotdiw tracker new writes the file to start from, generated from the interface. Two operations ship a tracker. The tap's formula no longer installs beads. Migration plan: a module written for 0.6.0 declares no interface and is read as interface 1; a checkout on beads goes on working while the binary is on the machine, and is told the one command when it is not.
updates.reason: A tracker could only be copied by hand into the home directory, which a package manager cannot write to, and nothing said which interface a module was written for.

updates.summary: The command line for operation.pour-procedure, and for the third step of operation.start-named-work, is now dotdiw formula pour <formula>, which dotdiw's own messages tell people to use. dotdiw mol pour <formula> still runs the same operations and prints the same. The operations, the tracker interface's pour-steps and what an adapter answers keep their names, because adapter files already implement them. Migration plan: none; both commands work.
updates.reason: mol pour is a name from beads. The other formula commands are formula new, formula list and formula show, so pouring now sits with them.

updates.summary: A new type, type.tracker-actor, holds the account a tracker writes work under: a name, the tracker's own id for it, and whether the tracker confirmed it. describe-tracker may return it as actor, and adopt-repository and use-tracker return it too, after asking describe-tracker. The item record gains an optional assignee, update-item can fail with assignee-not-found, and the responses of a migration gain assigneesLeft. The beads adapter reads git's user.name, so that call is declared on every operation that reaches it. The tracker interface keeps number 1, with its digest recorded again. Migration plan: none; every new field is optional, and an adapter written for interface 1 still passes tracker check, ten of ten.
updates.reason: Jira and beads write work under someone's name, and no record said whose, so dotdiw could not say it before work was written under the wrong name.

updates.summary: The kind of type.tracker-item becomes an enum of root and task, task when unsaid: the root a pour made is root and every other item is task, whatever the tracker calls it. create-item takes no kind, and neither do start-named-work and name-the-work. The tracker interface is number 2, with its digest recorded again, and a module written for 1 is refused in one line that names it. Migration plan: an adapter declares interface 2 and reads its tracker's own types as task; a local store's roots, recorded as molecule before 1.0.0, read as root.
updates.reason: dotdiw reads the kind for one thing, telling a poured root from a parent someone built by hand. While the kind was open, a root could be a molecule or an epic, and an epic someone built by hand could not be told from one.

updates.summary: type.held-formula gains verifyUsing, the means to prove a formula's run, as one-line strings. type.tracker-item gains description and verifyUsing, which pour-steps takes for the root, create-item takes for an item a move carries, and show-item returns exactly as given for any item; migrate-workspace reads each item whole with show-item and hands both over. The response of pour-procedure carries verifyUsing for the presenter, and a convention problem names a value check cannot read, one longer than a line, or a file of this repository that git does not track. Migration plan: none for formulas; the root's description and verifyUsing ride on tracker interface 2.
updates.reason: A formula said what to do and how its steps follow each other. Steps closed in order show that the order was kept; the means to prove show that the run did what the formula claims.

updates.summary: answer-through-a-formula-provider, register-provider, describe-provider, list-provider-formulas, show-provider-formula and remove-provider join the door, with type.formula-provider for a registered provider. type.held-formula gains provider, the name of the provider that serves the formula. index-the-project finds the local formulas on the file system, calls list-provider-formulas and show-provider-formula for each registered provider, and answers providersLeftOut, one line for each provider it left out of the run, and unparsed, the formula files it could not parse; a provider's formulas are indexed from its list, and resolve-formula calls show-provider-formula when a formula is shown or poured. resolve-formula answers a reason -- formula-not-found, ambiguous, provider-formula-unserved or provider-failed -- and pour-procedure's reason gains the last three, none of them handed to the tracker. type.formula-provider gains unavailable. Migration plan: a local formula whose id reads like a provider's suffixed id is renamed; nothing else moves.
updates.reason: A formula was a file that one repository's git tracked. Behind a formula management abstraction, where a formula is kept is the provider's business, and the door reaches every provider the same way.

updates.summary: list-formulas promises one header for every list, the number of formulas listed, where it promised "in this repo" while every formula listed was in the repository. No type moves. Migration plan: none.
updates.reason: The header kept 1.1's bytes for a list of local formulas only so that an old comparison held.

updates.summary: undo-earlier-adoption takes apply, and answers pending, one line for each thing an earlier version left, when it is not applied. Without apply it changes nothing and answers blocked while anything is left; adopt-a-repository calls it with apply before adopt-repository. Migration plan: run dotdiw init once in a checkout an earlier version adopted.
